entities.name: Dinner plate, glaze "Ochre Run" (autumn batch)
entities.description: Wheel-thrown stoneware dinner plate with a wide flat well and a low, slightly flared rim. Glaze breaks from ochre to near-white where it thins over the rim; iron speckle throughout. Raw, unglazed foot ring.
immutable_traits: wide flat well, low flared rim (no coupe shape)
glaze breaks lighter at the rim edge
visible iron speckle across the whole glazed surface
raw unglazed foot ring, slightly darker than the glaze
no decals, no printed pattern, no gold or metallic edge
allowed_variation: speckle density and placement (every piece differs)
glaze pooling depth in the well
use marks: crumbs, a smear of sauce, cutlery scuffs
forbidden_drift: recoloured glaze to match a palette swatch
scale drift: plate rendered as a side plate or a platter (dimensions UNKNOWN, see brand-system known_uncertainties.product_dimensions)

sources.quote: Glaze pools and speckles differ piece to piece, and that is the point.
Unglazed foot rings are left raw on purpose

entities.name: The long table by the glazing room window
entities.description: A scrubbed pale-oak trestle table, about three metres long, along a single tall north-facing window in the studio. Lime-washed wall behind; glaze buckets and ware boards just out of frame.
immutable_traits: pale scrubbed oak with knife marks and glaze drips
lime-washed off-white wall, no tiles, no shelving in frame
single window side: light always enters from one side
allowed_variation: bread, fruit, leftovers of a real meal
forbidden_drift: marble, terrazzo or polished concrete surfaces
kitchen islands, pendant lamps, open-plan show-home interiors
fake plants and decorative styling props

sources.ref: description assembled from the owner interview and listing photos; owner has not confirmed this location as the standard set

entities.name: North window, late afternoon
entities.description: Lighting recipe: one large soft source from the side (the north window), late afternoon so it is slightly warm and low. No fill card; the shadow side falls off into a soft grey so glaze depth reads. Exposure set for the glaze highlights, not the shadows.
immutable_traits: single soft key from one side, roughly 90 degrees to camera
no fill: shadow side open but unlit
highlights on glaze kept below clipping so speckle survives
no rim light, no visible strobes or reflectors
allowed_variation: key height from table level to 45 degrees
a thin bounce from the lime wall

sources.quote: 9 of 12 listing photos lit from one window side with open shadows
